nodes.description: The only curative treatment reported: matched family-donor transplants in early childhood with fludarabine-based reduced-intensity conditioning, and haploidentical transplants in older children after myeloid transformation. Because patient cells are hypersensitive to genotoxic agents, the reporting groups favour low-genotoxicity conditioning and caution with busulfan, cyclophosphamide and irradiation, by analogy with Fanconi anaemia. Timing balances transplant toxicity against the risk of later clonal evolution; the published series is too small to define it. Chronic GVHD of the eyes and lungs has been reported after haploidentical transplant.

evidence.snippet: Importantly, Mysm1(tm1a/tm1a) HSCs were functionally impaired, and this was associated with elevated levels of reactive oxygen species, γH2AX DNA damage marker, and p53 protein in the hematopoietic progenitors.

nodes.description: Mysm1-deficient mice show increased apoptosis in developing brain and skin, growth retardation, neurological defects, skin atrophy, tail malformation and osteopenia with shortened long bones, all rescued by p53 deletion. This is the proposed basis for the growth, neurodevelopmental and skeletal features in patients, but the human link is inferred from the mouse, not shown in patient tissue.

biological_processes: intrinsic apoptotic signaling pathway by p53 class mediator

evidence.reference_title: Interplay of H2A deubiquitinase 2A-DUB/Mysm1 and the p19(ARF)/p53 axis in hematopoiesis, early T-cell development and tissue differentiation.
evidence.snippet: Increased rates of apoptosis were also detected in other tissues affected by Mysm1 deficiency, including the developing brain and the skin.

evidence.reference_title: Interplay of H2A deubiquitinase 2A-DUB/Mysm1 and the p19(ARF)/p53 axis in hematopoiesis, early T-cell development and tissue differentiation.
evidence.snippet: defective B-cell development, growth retardation, neurological defects, skin atrophy, and tail malformation were almost completely restored as well

evidence.reference_title: Loss of p53 compensates osteopenia in murine Mysm1 deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Skeletal alterations and osteopenia of Mysm1-deficient mice were phenotypically completely rescued by simultaneous ablation of p53 in p53-/-Mysm1-/- double-deficient mice
